entries.subject: Rommel et al. (2025) occultation-constrained oblate model
entries.finding: The selected shape is the published primary-body oblate model with semiaxes a = b = 218.05 +/-0.11 km and c = 187.5 +/-2.4 km from the 2025 multi-event analysis; the satellite is excluded from the displayed primary dimensions.

entries.subject: Satellite-orbit pole used as a body-pole prior
entries.finding: The display uses the paper's J2000-equatorial satellite-orbit pole at right ascension 20.8 +/-1.9 degrees and declination 34.9 +/-1.9 degrees as a body-pole prior under the explicit equatorial-orbit assumption, with an arbitrary prime meridian and rotational phase.

entries.subject: Earlier 2019 occultation-only fits
entries.finding: The README keeps the earlier fits as supporting data only, because the 2025 paper reports timing and profile disagreements and poor Keplerian satellite-orbit fit quality.
entries.revisitWhen: A reanalysis reconciles the timing and profile disagreements or improves the satellite-orbit fit enough to change the adopted model.

entries.subject: Depth, flattening and hydrostatic interpretation
entries.finding: The depth and inferred flattening depend on the equatorial satellite-orbit assumption; the paper disfavours hydrostatic Maclaurin equilibrium and this view asserts none.
entries.revisitWhen: An independent pole determination or a direct measurement of the polar axis removes the equatorial-orbit assumption.

entries.subject: cssEarth missing-coverage grid as the surface
entries.finding: No surface imagery exists for this body, so the manifest supplies the project-authored missing-coverage grid, the normal grid marks unmapped terrain and Shadows defaults off; no satellite is fabricated in the body scene.
